speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; please describe exactly how your leg was positioned immediately after the impact and whether you heard a "pop" at the time of injury.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; could you tell me if your right hip is currently unable to move, specifically if you cannot rotate your leg inward or if your leg appears rotated outward compared to the other side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Hip Dislocation (Medial/Ipsilateral).

The clinical presentation of severe right groin pain with the right leg shortened, adducted, and internally rotated following a rear-end collision is pathognomonic for an anterior hip dislocation. I will request an X-ray to confirm the diagnosis and check for associated fractures. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Hip_XRay
